brief.job: Show the studio, the work, and how to reach him
brief.narrative: Name the studio, show shipped sites, then principles and contact
acceptance_checks: chat WhatsApp and LINE still work

Astro multi-page site instead of a single HTML file

content.tagline: Art and science share a bench.

features.name: The Lucid Lens
features.subtitle: Photographs that pretend.
features.description: A photography site that treats snapshots as if they were a curated portfolio. The joke is the point, and the pictures still have to hold.

features.name: Falling Tree Studio
features.subtitle: Furniture from the bench.
features.description: Wood and epoxy tables made by hand. The site is a gallery for pieces that already exist in the room, not a catalog of renders.

features.name: Tools that should exist
features.subtitle: Visa, timezone, weather, money.
features.description: Visa Cheat Sheet, Timezone Guru, Weather Wombat, and Retire Guru started because the existing options were sales copy or too dense to trust. They stay free.

features.name: Generative play
features.subtitle: Geometry and harmony.
features.description: Lucid Geometry extends Spirograph into interactive 3D. Lucid Musician trains a harmony model on centuries of composition. Art and science in the same loop.

principles.title: Static where static is enough
principles.description: Ship HTML first. Add a runtime only when the interaction needs it.

principles.title: Infrastructure lives with the app
principles.description: DNS, certificates, CDN, and deploy sit in CDK next to the site.

principles.title: AI removes drudgery
principles.description: Assistants help name, structure, and search. They do not become the product.

principles.title: Boring cloud, quiet scale
principles.description: S3, CloudFront, Route 53, Lambda, DynamoDB. Pieces that stay out of the way.

principles.title: Leave room for craft
principles.description: Photography, furniture, and music tools get the same care as the serious apps.

principles.title: Open source and free
principles.description: The sites are there to be used. Bugs and ideas are welcome by email.

faq.a: A personal studio site for Dinsor (Stephen Harrison). It is not an agency, a product company, or a theme shop.
Stephen Harrison. Locals in Bangkok call him ดินสอ (din-sɔ̌ɔ), meaning pencil. The passport and the bank use Stephen.
No. The public sites are free to use and open source. Contact above if you want to talk about something else.

faq.q: What kind of work is this?
faq.a: Photography, handmade furniture, and small web tools. The through-line is hands-on art and practical software with a clear purpose.

faq.q: How do I get in touch?
faq.a: Open Contact in the header for LINE, WhatsApp, and email at dinsor@dinsor.org. LinkedIn is in the footer.
Astro, TypeScript, Tailwind or CSS, React islands when needed, hosted on S3 and CloudFront via AWS CDK. The technology page has the notes.

footer.ethos: A pencil is for ideas on the go.
